paper_metadata.title: Recurrence After a First Untreated Seizure in the Hong Kong Chinese Population

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the setting well. However, it is a retrospective review of EEG laboratory referrals rather than a prospective community-based cohort. This sampling frame may miss patients who did not receive an EEG, potentially introducing selection bias toward more severe or clinically uncertain cases.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: We reviewed the records of 2938 referrals to the EEG laboratory from June 1993 to December 1996 at the Prince of Wales hospital in Hong Kong.
items.reasoning: The source population (EEG referrals in a specific hospital/region) is clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Three hundred ten (11%) requests were for a first unprovoked seizure (19); the remaining 2628 EEGs were for other indications
items.reasoning: While the identification method is clear (EEG logs), using EEG referrals as the primary sampling frame may exclude patients with first seizures who were not referred for an EEG, creating a potential selection bias.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: from June 1993 to December 1996
items.reasoning: The dates are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Prince of Wales hospital in Hong Kong... our hospital was the only publicly funded acute hospital in the district during the study period.
items.reasoning: The setting and its role in the local healthcare system are well-described.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria consisted of the following. (a) Only those with a definite witnessed attack consisting of an unprovoked generalized tonic-clonic seizure were included... (b) Patients were older than 14 years. (c) Antiepileptic medications were withheld after the first seizure.
items.reasoning: The criteria are detailed and include specific seizure types and age limits.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: We retrieved 310 records, of which 132 fulfilled the criteria as given here.
items.reasoning: While the flow from 310 to 132 is explained by criteria, it is unclear if all eligible patients in the hospital's catchment area were captured by the EEG referral system.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The male-to-female ratio was 1:1, and age ranged from 13 to 86 years, with a mean of 33 years.
items.reasoning: Basic demographics and clinical characteristics (EEG findings, CT results) are provided.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The loss to follow-up is very low (4 patients out of 132), and the reasons for death/loss are provided. The follow-up duration is sufficient for the outcome of interest.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Four patients had died... and four were lost to follow-up.
items.reasoning: Only 8 out of 132 patients (approx 6%) were lost, which is well within the acceptable range for low risk.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Relevant information... was derived from medical and computer records and from telephone interviews.
items.reasoning: The authors used multiple data sources to minimize loss.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: Four patients had died (two from pneumonia, one from a motor vehicle accident, and one from an unknown cause), and four were lost to follow-up.
items.reasoning: Specific reasons for death and the number of dropouts are stated.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not provide a comparison of baseline characteristics between those lost to follow-up and those who completed the study.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factors (EEG and CT) were measured using standard clinical protocols. The EEG reader was blinded to the outcome, which significantly reduces measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Standardized EEG findings consisted of a 30-min recording... Findings were classified into three groups: (a) focal or generalized epileptiform discharges... (b) localized nonepileptic activity... and (c) normal.
items.reasoning: The measurement and classification of the EEG (a key PF) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: EEGs were retrieved and read by one of the authors (C.F.H.), who had no access to the recurrence status of patients.
items.reasoning: Blinding of the EEG assessor to the outcome is a strong safeguard against bias.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: age ranged from 13 to 86 years, with a mean of 33 years.
items.reasoning: Age is treated as a continuous variable in the Cox model (Rate ratio 0.99).

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: EEG and routine blood tests are performed as part of the recommended work-up of every person with a first convulsion in our institution.
items.reasoning: Standardized protocols were used for all patients.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Brain CTs were performed in 85 (64%) of patients.
items.reasoning: While EEG data was complete, CT data was missing for 36% of the sample, which is a significant proportion.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Those without CT scans were included in the analysis except for the univariate analysis of abnormal CT imaging as a risk factor; in which case this was only performed for patients who had available scans.
items.reasoning: No imputation was used; the authors used available-case analysis, which can introduce bias if the reason for missing CTs is related to prognosis.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure recurrence) was partly determined via telephone interviews and retrospective record review. This relies on patient/witness recall and may lead to under-reporting of events, although the focus on generalized tonic-clonic seizures (which are harder to miss) mitigates this somewhat.

items.evidence_snippet: taking an event as the occurrence of a second seizure... Mean duration of follow-up was 27.2 months
items.reasoning: The outcome and follow-up duration are clearly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: Relevant information... whether a second seizure had occurred was derived from medical and computer records and from telephone interviews.
items.reasoning: Telephone interviews are subject to recall bias, though medical records provide some objective verification.

items.reasoning: Major known prognostic factors in epilepsy were collected.
